component.name: Carosello
component.summary: A fast, minimalist image and video viewer for Linux

description.p: Carosello is a fast, minimalist image and video viewer for Linux. It opens images and videos from a directory, lets you navigate between files with keyboard shortcuts or gestures, and displays them with zoom and pan capabilities.

screenshot.caption: Carosello viewing images with navigation controls

description.p: Automatically notify FlatPark when a GitHub release is published, so Flatpak users receive new versions without waiting for the daily update check.

Fix the touchpad double-click zoom sometimes jumping to the top-left corner, and greatly reduce skipped slide transitions when swiping: the neighbor prefetch now starts with each slide, and the frame you just left is kept for a quick swipe back.

Escape now leaves fullscreen (it still resets the zoom when you are not in fullscreen). Move to Trash falls back to a direct delete on filesystems without a Trash, such as remote sftp/smb mounts. Built on the GNOME 50 runtime.

Rotate/mirror tools with in-place autosave, an optional two-finger swipe navigation gesture, double-click zoom anchored at the cursor, faster worker-thread image decoding with cancellable prefetching, and a Flatpak now built on the GNOME 51 runtime.
Arch Linux packaging (PKGBUILD/AUR), full image/video file associations, and single-source versioning across Cargo, Meson, Flatpak and Arch.

Slide animation between items (3-finger drag follows the finger), Preferences switch to disable it, sandboxed drag-and-drop of portal files and folders, and EXIF-orientation fix for transition frames.
Move the current item to Trash with Del, staying on the next item instead of resetting to the first.
Embed CSS in the binary so release artifacts are styled without an installed GResource bundle.
Fix flatpak: remove DBusActivatable without service file.
Fix CI: correct libadwaita/gtk requirements and flatpak finish-args.
Fit media to window and handle resize; HIG improvements.
Bugfixes and GNOME HIG compliance improvements.
